answer: Bounded seat register: every identity must hold one of a fixed number of non-transferable mining seats. A farm of n clones needs n seats, bid from a supply that never grows, and each seat is sunk because it cannot be resold. A per-operator cap, enforced by saffron-flagged audits drawn from unrelated cohorts, stops any cartel short of its zenith: hoarding only inflates what they already paid. So each extra clone costs more than the last, and pooling buys nothing. Small as an opal, hard to split.
